channel.title: Void News: On Air

item.title: Russia Attacks Ukraine; Black Sea Drones; Colombia Shifts Israel Policy: On Air, October 14, 2026
item.description:
Russia launched aerial attacks targeting Ukrainian cities and power plants on October 14, 2026. This occurred hours after the Kremlin stated the scope of US President Donald Trump's proposed energy ceasefire was unclear. Trump unilaterally announced an energy ceasefire on October 11, 2026, without outlining its scope. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the continued Russian attacks a show of disregard for the Trump-backed truce.
Elon Musk’s SpaceX limited Ukraine’s access to its Starlink satellite service without warning on Wednesday, disrupting combat drone operations. SpaceX introduced a speed limit for Starlink terminals in motion, capping the velocity of Ukrainian drones at 100 miles per hour. Presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov complained Ukraine’s defense forces received no warning about these restrictions. The Starlink restrictions coincided with a new wave of Russian ballistic missile and drone attacks on Ukraine.
Bulgaria stated on Wednesday that Russia was likely behind drone attacks that struck four vessels in the Black Sea over the past week. Rescuers continue to search for 11 missing crew members after strikes on Tuesday sank two ships in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone and adjacent waters. Five other crew members were rescued. One of the sunken ships is registered to Guinea-Bissau, while the other, the Chelsea-3, is Ukrainian-owned.
Yemen's Houthi rebels launched new attacks on Saudi Arabia, striking the headquarters of national oil giant Aramco in Dhahran and targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The Saudi-led coalition announced it intercepted a ballistic missile over Riyadh on Wednesday. The Houthis vowed to continue targeting Saudi airports and oil infrastructure in retaliation for "Saudi aggression" against Yemen's capital, Sanaa. The Saudi Ministry of Energy confirmed a limited fire in an administrative building at Aramco.
Colombia opened its embassy in Jerusalem on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, becoming the 10th country to establish a diplomatic mission in the city. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar and Colombian Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar attended the inauguration ceremony. The move reverses the policy of former Colombian President Gustavo Petro, who severed diplomatic relations with Israel in May 2024. Petro had also terminated a free trade agreement with Israel in October 2024; Colombia restored this agreement.
Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay on Wednesday condemned President Donald Trump’s sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC). Pillay described the US sanctions as "illegal" and "unlawful" interference with an independent international court. The US announced sanctions against the ICC on Friday, aimed at disrupting its day-to-day operations. These sanctions will take effect in six months.
United States federal agents arrested Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi national, and charged him with planting a hidden audio recording device in a conference room at the California offices of OpenAI. Alfozan, 35, had been working at the AI company as an engineer since July 2025. OpenAI discovered a sophisticated recording device plugged into a USB port behind a television in an executive conference room at one of its San Francisco buildings on September 30. The device was concealed in toilet paper.
U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly ruled Tuesday that CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are likely to succeed in their constitutional free speech and due process claims. Judge Kelly extended an order blocking President Donald Trump from banning them from the White House. A preliminary injunction issued late Tuesday extends White House press access indefinitely for the three news outlets.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: Saudi Strikes Escalate, Black Sea Shipping Hit, IMF Warns AI Risks: On Air, October 13, 2026
item.description:
Saudi Arabia struck an oil facility near Sanaa on Tuesday, according to Yemen’s Houthi movement, following an evacuation warning from the Saudi-led coalition. An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported hearing an explosion. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree threatened to target Riyadh’s international airport, a refinery, and an Aramco facility in Dammam if Saudi forces continued. A Houthi missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday killed 13 people and wounded over 300. U.S. President Donald Trump condemned the Houthi actions, suggesting they aim to drive up oil prices.
Suspected Russian drones struck two cargo ships off Bulgaria on Tuesday, sinking one vessel and prompting Bulgaria to summon the Russian ambassador. The Guinea-Bissau flagged cargo vessel HS Dignity sank 17 nautical miles east of Krapets, leaving 11 sailors missing after five were rescued. The Bulgarian interior ministry stated the ship was traveling between Algeria and the Romanian port of Braila with Syrian and Egyptian nationals. Arab News Pakistan and RTE News also reported the Chelsea 3 was hit 16 nautical miles east of Byala.
Greta Thunberg joined protesters outside Lycée Paul Eluard in Saint-Denis, north of Paris, on Tuesday. French pupils demonstrated for a fourth week over poor learning conditions, including teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms, and crumbling school buildings. The nationwide protest movement involves marches, blockades of hundreds of schools, and clashes with police in Strasbourg, Nantes, and Lyon.
French investigators hunt hackers who seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets in a cyberattack overnight from October 11 to October 12. No group has publicly claimed responsibility, and no ransom demand has been made, puzzling investigators. The cyberattack impacted at least 350 supermarkets, spoiling large quantities of fresh and frozen food and leading to millions of euros in losses. Many affected refrigeration units relied on outdated firmware from Danish firm Danfoss.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) raised its global growth forecast for 2026 to 3.1%, attributing this to strong AI infrastructure investment offsetting higher oil prices. The IMF's World Economic Outlook (WEO) report also predicts 3.4% global growth in 2027, assuming the Strait of Hormuz reopens by March. The IMF warned of risks to global growth and financial stability, including a potential end to the AI investment boom and a prolonged Middle East conflict.
President Trump praised Somaliland at an Ohio rally, referring to it as a "totally different country" from Somalia. This occurred days after Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi spoke with Breitbart News. Trump also attacked Somali immigrants, warning that Democrats would allow states to be flooded with migrants from places like Somalia. He specifically mentioned Rep. Ilhan Omar, calling her a disaster.
The United States Supreme Court agreed to hear arguments in a legal battle over the transparency and operational authority of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW) brought the lawsuit, seeking public records related to DOGE's activities during early 2025. The central dispute is whether DOGE is a federal agency subject to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) or a presidential advisory body exempt from FOIA requirements.
Indigenous Peoples' Day was celebrated on October 12 with various events across the United States. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) posted on social media celebrating "Native Americans' Day" in South Dakota. Indigenous activist Leonard Peltier vowed resistance against Trump administration policies affecting tribal rights and sovereignty.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: US Sanctions Shift, UK Realigns, Israel Border Explodes: On Air, October 12, 2026
item.description:
President Donald Trump authorized Russian diesel imports, temporarily lifting sanctions via an OFAC license. A White House official asserts the additional supply will lower prices for American farmers and truckers, though energy experts express skepticism that existing customers will seek fuel elsewhere, keeping prices stable. A bipartisan group of US senators called on the administration to reverse the deal, which US envoys reportedly told Ukrainian officials aims to draw Russia back to peace talks.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) almost certainly directed a security incident at RAF Fairford, a base used by the United States Air Force. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced immediate asset freezes and travel bans for Ruhollah Bazghandi, identified as the IRGC's head of counterespionage operations, and Shahram Ali Reza Tamarzadeh Jakki, a facilitator of hostile activity. The Iranian ambassador to the UK was summoned to the Foreign Office.
An unexploded cluster munition, believed to be from the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah, detonated in northern Israel, killing one 14-year-old student and injuring 24 others. The incident occurred during an annual school trip near Mitzpe Be’er and Ramim Ridge.
U.S. District Judge Jennifer L. Rochon ordered the Trump administration to cancel remaining taxpayer-funded television commercials promoting his political message. The judge issued a temporary restraining order, effective for two weeks, prohibiting the development, creation, dissemination, placement, or airing of the challenged advertisements, for which the Department of Homeland Security allocated $20 million.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to renegotiate parts of the post-Brexit trade deal with the European Union, stating the existing relationship is "not good enough. Burnham confirmed he will attend a bilateral summit in Brussels on November 20, aiming to make progress on issues such as boosting UK growth, controlling illegal immigration, and emissions trading.
U.S. federal agents searched the Washington home of Democratic U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar as part of a criminal investigation conducted by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents. Omar stated on X the search was an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.
These measures include asset freezes and travel bans, with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas describing it as the largest expansion of the sanctions list since the war in Ukraine began.
North Korea launched multiple ballistic missiles toward the sea off its eastern coast, following South Korea's hypersonic missile test on October 8. South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff detected the launches from the Pyongyang area, with at least one missile traveling more than 900 kilometers.
The INDIA bloc conducted a "March for Democracy" in Delhi, culminating in a Supreme Court petition challenging the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and naming Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as a respondent. The Supreme Court registry identified multiple defects in the petition, including a shortfall in court fees of over Rs 200 and missing documents.
Columbus Day is observed as a federal holiday on October 12, 2026, with President Donald Trump issuing a message stating the days of plunder of statues are over and emphasizing the holiday's importance for the Italian American community. Indigenous Peoples' Day is also observed, often on the same day.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.
